podcast.title: Definition and Distinction
podcast.body: A rock opera, like traditional opera, is fundamentally a story told entirely through singing. This distinguishes it from rock musical theater, which typically incorporates spoken dialogue alongside songs. "In essence, a rock opera, like traditional opera, is a story that isn't told entirely through singing while musical theater usually has spoken dialogue as well as songs."

podcast.title: Early Candidate: A Man Dies
podcast.body: Ryan Fertel, a historian and author of a book in the 33 1/3 series on Drive-By Truckers' *Southern Rock Opera*, argues for "A Man Dies" as the first rock opera. He describes this early 1960s work as an attempt to stage the New Testament for the "boomer generation of rock and roll mad teenagers," addressing significant societal issues such as racism and poverty. "He makes a very compelling case for a man dies, which he described as an early 1960s attempt to stage the new testament for the boomer generation of rock and roll mad teenagers."

podcast.title: Format Definition
podcast.body: A rock opera is a type of concept album designed with the structure and narrative ambition of a traditional opera, but performed using rock music. "Not only was this a concept album, but it was designed as a full blown rock opera."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins as Serious Art Form
podcast.body: The rock opera genre emerged in the 1960s, driven by a desire for rock music to be recognized and taken seriously as an art form. This ambition was notably demonstrated by The Who, who daringly sought to produce work on a scale comparable to Wagnerian opera, a venture that proved successful with their fans. "Like so many things in the 70s, the rock opera was born in the 60s and it's part of this desire for the genre of rock music to be taken seriously as an art form. Really, it was incredibly balsy of the who that think that they could produce something on the scale of Wagner and that their fans would buy it, but it worked."

podcast.title: Thematic Focus on Youth
podcast.body: Classic rock operas frequently explore the "trials and tribulations of youth." This thematic connection makes the rock opera an ideal vehicle for a dramatic interpretation of life, particularly in the 70s, an era characterized by self-reflection. "They can. And an examination of some of the classic rock operas shows that they are, in fact, examining the trials and tribulations of youth."
